outcome: opioid consumption (measured by morphine equivalency rate - MER)
cohort: The study included 744 pediatric surgical patients evaluated by the acute pain service during a 6-month period at a large quaternary-care pediatric hospital, 333 of whom received regional anesthesia.
finding: The regional anesthesia group consumed significantly lower amounts of opioids compared to the non-regional anesthesia group over the night of surgery and in the post-operative days, with a notable proportion of RA patients needing no IV opioids.
